answer: One concrete defense is random-assignment peer bonding. When an agent joins, the network pairs it with a randomly chosen established member who must lock a copper-denominated collateral bond; if the newcomer is later proven fraudulent, that bond is slashed. Because pairings are unpredictable, an operator cannot route its own clones to a friendly voucher — each fake needs a stranger willing to risk real capital. Honest agents climb the trust summit together, while a sybil swarm is marooned on an island, unable to find anyone to bond it.
